clue.text: Waggish pair? Neither owns to being criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters before it are twisted out of their order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Two jokers deny any part in a crime, each refusing to own up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Two Ronnies were Ronnie Barker and Ronnie Corbett, a long-running British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic duo were famous for their wordplay and sketches, so 'waggish pair' describes the double act.

clue.text: Fancy stripe worn by corps – an army feature?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests elaborate rearrangement of the word that follows
the military letter goes in among the rearranged letters, the two worn together as one

blocks.note: anagram fodder
C is a standard abbreviation for corps

explanation.surface: A decorative stripe on a soldier's uniform sounds like a mark of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' is to be read as arm-y: a feature of the arm, not of the military. That is the pun the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm, so it is a feature of an arm.

clue.text: Face matter occupying uppity Frenchman

indicators.note: in a down clue something uppity goes upward, so the name is read from bottom to top
one word occupies another by sitting inside it

blocks.note: to matter is to count
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A haughty Frenchman faces up to some matter of business.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a problem or opponent is to encounter it, meet it head on; both are verbs.

clue.text: Rubbish picked up in part of frame

indicators.note: picked up means caught by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: rubbish is waste, which is pronounced the same as the answer

explanation.surface: Refuse is collected from part of a building's framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame' looks like scaffolding or a picture frame; here it means the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's frame is their body, and the waist is the part of it between ribs and hips.

clue.text: A lot of split rubber beginning to thin and burn

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the word loses its end
the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: to rive is to split or tear apart
the ule is a Central American rubber tree
first letter of thin

explanation.surface: Most of a split rubber starts to wear thin and burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' is not fire: in Scotland and northern England a burn is a small stream. ULE, a rubber tree, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivulet is a very small stream, which is what a burn is in Scots usage.

clue.text: How one might describe carnival hater's response to American – worthy of shame?

blocks.clueFragment: How one might describe carnival hater's response
blocks.note: someone who hates carnival would say no to Rio, home of the famous carnival
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes carnival snubs an American, and the reply is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three words, NO TO RIO, then add US.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, so a notorious person is one deserving of shame.

clue.text: Start of work among plain troops

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, after the pl and before ops

explanation.surface: Work begins among ordinary soldiers on a plain.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music or writing, its start.

clue.text: Song mostly well revised and expanded

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the final letter of that word drops away
a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: A song that was mostly fine has been revised and lengthened.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen means enlarged or puffed up, so something swollen has expanded in size.

clue.text: It's used for galvanising last character in college

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
taken as written
C is a standard abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: The last person to arrive at college galvanises the place into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galvanising' sounds like rousing someone, but here it is the industrial coating of steel.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanising coats iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc to stop rust.

clue.text: Request at home before formal call is denied

indicators.note: when something is denied it is refused, so those two letters are withheld from the longer word

blocks.note: at home means in
a visitation is an official visit
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Someone at home asks for a formal visit, which is refused.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitation is a polite request that someone come or take part, so it is a kind of request.

clue.text: Republican for all to see in stormy battle supplying contrary argument

indicators.note: something stormy is turbulent and churned up, so the word that follows is jumbled
in places one piece inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: R is short for Republican
anagram fodder
U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A Republican fighting a stormy public battle puts forward an opposing case.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal viewing, open to all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is an argument that refutes or contradicts another, a counter-argument.

clue.text: In part, young child is lacking time for grub

indicators.note: In tells us the shortened child goes inside the following word
lacking something means being without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: an actor's part is a role
a tot is a small child
T is short for time, removed from the child

explanation.surface: An infant playing a small role has no time to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, but here it is the verb: to dig or search about. 'In part' means inside the word for part, not a hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rootle is to rummage or dig about, as a pig does with its snout, which is to grub.

clue.text: Group of workers engaged in drink and short exercise

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so the workers sit inside the drink

blocks.note: a sip is a small drink
TU stands for trade union

explanation.surface: Union members are busy with a drink and a quick workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-up is a brief abdominal exercise of raising the torso from lying flat.

clue.text: Asian and a son in outfit beset by a lot of fear

indicators.note: in puts the letter for son inside the clothing word
beset means surrounded, so the fear word wraps round the rest
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
S is short for son
kit is an outfit of clothing
panic is sudden fear, cut to its first four letters

explanation.surface: An Asian man and his son in costume are gripped by dread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of fear' is the shortened word that besets the rest, so trim the fear before wrapping it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani is a person from Pakistan, a country in South Asia, so an Asian.

clue.text: Character touring storage facility with book, source of notes

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the first word encircles the next ones

blocks.note: the tone of a place is its character
ROM is read-only memory, computer storage
B is short for book

explanation.surface: A literary figure tours a warehouse with a book that gives them notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombone is a brass instrument, something that produces musical notes.

clue.text: Banger is falling apart traversing European body of water

indicators.note: something falling apart breaks up, so those letters are rearranged
traversing means stretching across, so the rearranged letters span the European letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder; a banger is British slang for a battered old car
E is short for European

explanation.surface: A clapped-out old car falls to pieces while crossing a stretch of European water.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger here is British slang for an old car, not a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bering Sea is the part of the North Pacific between Alaska and Russia, a body of water.

clue.text: Conservative idol largely enthusiastic or one found with reservations?

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the final letter of that word drops off

blocks.note: C is short for Conservative
an idol is a hero
keen means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A Tory idol is mostly keen, or perhaps someone with doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservations' looks like doubts; it means the lands reserved for Native American peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people, many of whom live on reservations in the US.

clue.text: School right to leave hospital garbage

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right departs, so its letters are taken out

blocks.note: Hogwarts is Harry Potter's school of wizardry
RT is an abbreviation for right, removed from the school
H is short for hospital

explanation.surface: The school's top person quits the hospital, which is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash means nonsense, worthless talk, so it is garbage in the figurative sense.

clue.text: A defender of cream?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone standing up for dairy cream, perhaps against health critics
setter's reading: the cream is the best of society, the select few, and this person champions them

explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' as in 'the cream of society' means the elite, the best people.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate of rule or privilege by a select upper class defends the favoured few, the cream of society.

clue.text: Sudden increase in fabric, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

blocks.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth

explanation.surface: A rise in sales of a certain cloth, so it is rumoured.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden powerful rise, as in a surge of demand or of electricity.

clue.text: Proper doctor coming up to admit first of those horribly injured

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of each following word
in a down clue coming up means reading from bottom to top
to admit is to let in, so the initials go inside

blocks.note: the initial letters of the three words
to doctor a drink is to lace it, add something to it

explanation.surface: A proper doctor arrives to admit the first of the badly hurt patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb: to tamper with or spike, as in lacing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical means morally right, in line with principles of conduct, so proper.

clue.text: Hairdresser generally on reflection concealed a means of leaving

indicators.note: concealed says the letters lie tucked within the words before it
a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A hairdresser, thinking it over, usually hid a way out.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, a way out of a place, so a means of leaving.

clue.text: English bird I ignored in uniform

indicators.note: the letter I is ignored, left out of the bird

blocks.note: E is short for English
the quail is a small game bird
taken as written, and removed

explanation.surface: A man in uniform ignores an English bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing; here it is the adjective meaning the same throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means consistent, the same in every part, which is what equal can mean.

clue.text: Staged work represented in a hotel

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A play is performed in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe is an operetta, a theatrical work written to be performed on stage.

clue.text: Means for turning in old part of county

blocks.note: first meaning: a machine that spins wood or metal for shaping
second meaning: a former administrative division of Kent

explanation.surface: A way of turning round in an old area of the shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent, a county in south-east England, was historically divided into lathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking machine rotates a workpiece for shaping, and historic Kent had districts with this name.

clue.text: One exposed to view touring a lake?

definitions.text: One exposed to view touring a lake?

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the nudist wraps round the next letters

blocks.note: a naturist goes without clothes, on full view
A taken as written, L short for lake

explanation.surface: A nudist strolls round a lake for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes someone studying wildlife on a lakeside walk, with the view being nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturalist studies plants and animals, so might tour a lake to view its wildlife.

clue.text: Dismiss old wine

blocks.note: first meaning: fire from a job
second meaning: a dry white wine imported from Spain in the 16th and 17th centuries

explanation.walkthrough: Sack is the old name for sherry-like wine, as drunk by Falstaff in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for firing an employee and a historical name for fortified Spanish white wine.

clue.text: Source of funds and wealth in Hello under review

indicators.note: something under review is being reworked and reconsidered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Celebrity riches feature in Hello! magazine, which is being reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine; a hole in the wall is British slang for a cash machine (ATM).
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine set into a bank's outside wall dispenses money, so it is a source of funds.
